# `WebSocket`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.WebSocket — outbound WebSocket client.

Opens a long-lived bidirectional connection to a peer.  Incoming
frames surface as `Sub` events on a Ipe.Web update loop (mirror
of `Ipe.Http.Stream.chunks`); outbound `send` writes a text
or binary frame from the calling goroutine.

Driving use cases: bidirectional LLM chat, collab editor ops,
multiplayer game state, financial feeds.  When you need request
/response with no incremental body Http.get is the right tool;
this is for the long-lived bidirectional case.

URLs must be `ws://` or `wss://` (prefer `wss://` for encrypted
connections).  Build a `WsUrl` via `WebSocket.url` — a plain
`String` or an `http://` URL is a type error.

Dial rule: a URL with `\` anywhere, or `@` in its path or fragment, is
refused (its credentials could run into the host) — write `@` as `%40`.
An `@` in the query is allowed, but an error for that URL then withholds
the host.

Lifecycle:

 1. `Cmd.perform (WebSocket.connect wsUrl) Connected` — kick
    off the handshake.  The runtime returns a `WebSocket` once the
    handshake completes (no message wait).

 2. `subscriptions model = WebSocket.onMessage sock GotFrame` —
    subscribe to incoming frames.  Each `Text String` or
    `Binary String` Msg flows through `update`.

 3. `WebSocket.send sock "hello"` — write a text frame.  Blocks
    up to 30 s if the underlying write buffer is full.

 4. `WebSocket.close sock` — release the connection.  Idempotent.

Session lifecycle: when a Ipe.Web session is evicted (TTL OR
explicit Delete) the runtime closes every owned socket
automatically — app code is NEVER responsible for cleanup on
disconnect.

Heartbeat: built-in ping every 30 s by default (configurable via
`connectWith.pingInterval`).  A peer that doesn't pong within
the timeout triggers `onClose` automatically.

Backpressure: `send` blocks up to the consumer-stall timeout
(30 s).  The bounded read channel (64 frames) provides
per-socket backpressure to the upstream when the user's update
loop falls behind — Ipe.Web's existing
`ipe_web_sse_drops_total` covers spillover.

See `examples/33-websocket-echo` for the canonical pattern.

## `WebSocket`

Opaque handle to an open WebSocket.  The wrapped `Int` is the
runtime's per-socket id; user code treats it as opaque.

## `WebSocketMessage`

One incoming frame from the peer.

  * `Text String` — UTF-8 text frame.
  * `Binary Bytes` — raw byte frame (`Vec<u8>` on Rust).

## `CloseCode`

A WebSocket close code.  Either one of the standard symbolic
codes OR a `Custom Int` for application-defined codes (1000-4999).

## `WsUrl`

An opaque WebSocket URL.  The ONLY way to build one is `WebSocket.url`,
which accepts a `Ipe.Url.Url` and rejects any scheme other than `ws` or
`wss`.  A non-WebSocket URL is a construction-time `Err`, never a value
that reaches a live socket.  Prefer `wss://` for encrypted connections.

## `url`

```ipe
url : Url -> Result Error WsUrl
```

`url u` — the parse-don't-validate seal for WebSocket URLs.  Returns `Ok`
when `u`'s scheme is `"ws"` or `"wss"`, otherwise `Err`.

## `toUrl`

```ipe
toUrl : WsUrl -> Url
```

`toUrl wsUrl` — recover the underlying `Url` (e.g. to read the host).

## `WebSocketCfg`

Connect configuration record for `connectWith`.

Every typed record ships with a `default` constructor + `with*`
builder helpers so adding new fields in future releases doesn't
break downstream record literals.

## `defaultCfg`

```ipe
defaultCfg : WsUrl -> WebSocketCfg
```

Default WebSocketCfg.  All-defaults values.  Override fields
with the `with*` builder helpers.  The time-span defaults come from the typed
`defaultTimeout`, unwrapped to milliseconds only here at the DTO boundary, so
no bare `30000` literal survives in the surface.

## `withHeaders`

```ipe
withHeaders : List ( String, String ) -> WebSocketCfg -> WebSocketCfg
```

Override the HTTP headers (e.g. Authorization) sent on the
upgrade handshake.

## `withTimeout`

```ipe
withTimeout : Duration -> WebSocketCfg -> WebSocketCfg
```

Override the handshake timeout (default 30 s).  Takes a typed
`Ipe.Duration` (e.g. `Duration.seconds 30`); the raw milliseconds are
unwrapped into the transport DTO for the runtime.

## `withPingInterval`

```ipe
withPingInterval : Duration -> WebSocketCfg -> WebSocketCfg
```

Override the ping interval (default 30 s).  Takes a typed `Ipe.Duration`;
`Duration.zero` disables application-level pings entirely.  The raw
milliseconds are unwrapped into the transport DTO for the runtime.

## `connect`

```ipe
connect : WsUrl -> Task Error WebSocket
```

`connect wsUrl` — open a new WebSocket to `wsUrl` (`ws://` or `wss://`).
The `WsUrl` constructor rejects any other scheme at construction time, so
a non-WebSocket address is a type error, never a runtime surprise.  The
Task resolves once the handshake completes; frames flow via `onMessage`
after that.  A handshake past the size limit fails the Task with a
`LimitExceeded` error.

## `connectWith`

```ipe
connectWith : WebSocketCfg -> Task Error WebSocket
```

`connectWith cfg` — connect with custom headers / timeout /
ping cadence.  Build the cfg via `defaultCfg url |> withHeaders
[...]` etc. so future field additions don't break call sites.

## `send`

```ipe
send : WebSocket -> String -> Task Error ()
```

`send sock text` — write a text frame.  Blocks up to 30 s if
the write buffer is full.

## `sendBinary`

```ipe
sendBinary : WebSocket -> Bytes -> Task Error ()
```

`sendBinary sock bytes` — write a binary frame.  Takes `Bytes`
(a distinct primitive in this backend, unlike the reference's
String alias — sanctioned divergence §B18).

## `close`

```ipe
close : WebSocket -> Task Error ()
```

`close sock` — release the connection (sends a Normal close
frame).  Idempotent.

## `closeWithCode`

```ipe
closeWithCode : CloseCode -> String -> WebSocket -> Task Error ()
```

`closeWithCode code reason sock` — release the connection with
a custom close code + reason.

## `onOpen`

```ipe
onOpen : WebSocket -> msg -> Sub msg
```

`onOpen sock msg` — dispatch `msg` once the socket is connected.
The Sub is one-shot semantically (the connection opens at most
once over its lifetime); subsequent re-subscriptions are no-ops.

## `onMessage`

```ipe
onMessage : WebSocket -> (WebSocketMessage -> msg) -> Sub msg
```

`onMessage sock toMsg` — dispatch `toMsg event` for every
incoming frame.

## `onClose`

```ipe
onClose : WebSocket -> (CloseCode -> msg) -> Sub msg
```

`onClose sock toMsg` — dispatch `toMsg closeCode` when the
peer (or this side) closes the connection.

## `onError`

```ipe
onError : WebSocket -> (Error -> msg) -> Sub msg
```

`onError sock toMsg` — dispatch `toMsg err` on a network /
protocol error.  A message or frame past `IPE_WS_MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES`
dispatches a `LimitExceeded` error.  The socket is closed automatically
after the error is dispatched.
